name: Tabelo
tagline: Edit one table visually or as text, entirely in your browser.
description: A table editor where the grid and the text formats stay in sync: Markdown, CSV, TSV, JSON, HTML and Jira. Everything runs locally as a PWA, so no table you paste ever leaves your machine.

image.alt: Tabelo showing the same table as Markdown text on the left and as an editable grid on the right

cardAlt: Tabelo on a denim card: the Markdown and Table panes of one workspace showing the same table of cities, kept in sync.

name: Mailbell
tagline: Gmail notifications in the macOS menu bar, with no server in between.
description: Instant IMAP IDLE alerts for Gmail, a review queue you can clear in one click, and OAuth with PKCE stored in the Keychain. The app talks to Gmail directly; nothing of yours passes through anyone else's machine.
discontinuedReason: Gmail now reaches me through Beeper.
cardAlt: The Mailbell bell icon and the words Free for Mac, open source, Mailbell, Gmail notifications in your menu bar, beside a drawing of the Mailbell menu: Accounts, three messages awaiting review, All Messages, Check Now, Settings and Quit Mailbell.

name: Meantime
tagline: World clocks in the macOS menu bar, with time travel.
description: Scheduled clocks, a quick calendar, and a slider that moves every clock at once so you can find a meeting time across time zones without arithmetic. Native, fast and private.

image.alt: Meantime's menu bar panel with two city clocks and a calendar

cardAlt: The Meantime clock icon and the words Free for Mac, open source, Meantime, World clocks in your menu bar, beside the Meantime panel with two clocks and a month calendar.

name: AtlasTint
tagline: An interactive SVG atlas for colouring and tracking regions of the world.
description: Select countries and regions, give them colours, and keep the result locally. Built on D3 and TopoJSON with keyboard navigation for every region, because a map you can only use with a mouse is only half a map.
cardAlt: The AtlasTint mark and the words Free in your browser, AtlasTint, Color and track the regions of the world, beside a drawing of the app: the Regions list and a world map with Canada and Brazil colored in.

name: Todo Print
tagline: Design and print to-do lists as exact-size A4 layouts.
description: A visual or Markdown editor for structured checklists that prints exactly as laid out, offline, with the layout stored on your machine. For people who still like paper.
discontinuedReason: Google Tasks can now print lists.
cardAlt: Todo Print on a graphite card: an A4 landscape sheet with three panels of to-do lists, headings and checkboxes, ready to print.

name: WindowHop
tagline: Switch between windows, not just apps, on macOS.
description: A native macOS window switcher with large app icons or live previews, bound to a keyboard shortcut. Free, GPL-licensed, no telemetry. Built because Command-Tab switches apps and I wanted to switch windows.

image.alt: WindowHop's switcher with a grid of window previews and their app icons

cardAlt: The WindowHop icon and the words Free for Mac, open source, WindowHop, Switch between windows, not just apps, beside a drawing of the switcher panel with eight window previews.

name: Smart Desk
tagline: Today's tasks and calendar in one native Apple app.
description: A day-focused planner for iPhone and Mac: app-owned tasks in Core Data synced through CloudKit, alongside Apple Calendar events read from EventKit and cached for offline use. Local-first, offline-first, and built for my own day.
note: Personal app, never released. Its page describes what it did.
discontinuedReason: Replaced by Leve and Google Tasks.
cardAlt: Smart Desk on a green card: the Mac window with its sidebar and the day list, calendar events and tasks together under an upcoming-event banner.

name: Orbit
tagline: Google Contacts, grouped by place, on the iPhone.
description: A personal iOS app for managing Google Contacts: import Apple Contacts into Google, group people by city and country, and search a fast local-first cache of everyone you know. Built for my own address book and not published.
note: Personal app, not released. The page says what it will do.

image.alt: Orbit's app icon, two overlapping white circles on green

cardAlt: Orbit on a teal card: two iPhone screens, contacts grouped by country and city, and a map with each contact pinned where they live.
discontinuedReason: No longer maintained; its page stays in the archive.

name: Country Badge Generator
tagline: Downloadable SVG, PNG and JPG country badges from flag colours.
description: Pick a country, get a badge with one of three deterministic, flag-inspired backgrounds, and download it in the format you need. Plain JavaScript, no build step, tested end to end with Playwright.
cardAlt: Country Badge Generator on an emerald card: Brazil selected, three flag-colour backgrounds, SVG, PNG and JPG formats and a large badge preview.

name: Issues Graph
tagline: See the blocking order of a GitHub backlog as a graph.
description: Reads issue dependencies through the GitHub API and lays them out as a directed graph in the browser, with nothing installed in the repository being read. Useful for finding what to unblock first.
discontinuedReason: No longer maintained; its last build stays in the archive.
cardAlt: Issues Graph on a graphite card: a chain of four GitHub issues, one ready, two blocked and one needing attention, joined by blocker-to-dependent arrows.

name: Moon Uniform
tagline: An open font family for the Moon tactile alphabet.
description: Moon is the raised alphabet William Moon published in 1845 for people who lose their sight later in life. This font draws the script, applies the historical short-form rules to plain English through OpenType features, and cites a source for every sign. Three weights, a dot-matrix variant for embossers, and a specimen with a type tester.

image.alt: The words Moon Uniform set in the Moon tactile alphabet, green on cream

cardAlt: Moon Uniform on a forest-green card: a specimen sheet with the word Moon and the letters A to Z set in the Moon alphabet.

name: Lights
tagline: A small society of lights that drift together, fall out and fade in the dark.
description: An ambient agent-based simulation on a canvas: the lights move, form bonds, grow old and occasionally say something through the Web Speech API. No build, no dependencies, one HTML file.

image.alt: Small points of light drifting across a dark field

cardAlt: Lights, generative art: a frame of the piece, small white, blue and amber lights and the faint trails of two bonds drifting in the night.

name: Linguae
tagline: Every documented language in the Wikitongues database, in one table.
description: An interactive table for exploring the world's linguistic diversity, fed by the Wikitongues Airtable base. A side project born from a hobby.
discontinuedReason: No longer maintained; its last build stays in the archive.
cardAlt: Linguae on a rose card: the language table with its filters, codes and status chips such as vigorous, threatened and endangered.

name: Ink Tools
tagline: Unofficial plugins and Mac tools for Supernote e-ink tablets.
description: Tablet plugins that sync calendars and to-dos, look up a handwritten word, edit pictures and send pages over LocalSend, with a Mac app that opens .note notebooks and a command line that drives the tablet. Unofficial and not made by Ratta: Supernote names only the device it runs on.

image.alt: The Ink Tools icon: a pen nib writing one stroke on a light page, on an ink-grey tile

cardAlt: Ink Tools on an ink-blue card: a Supernote page with a lassoed handwritten word, the Lasso Actions buttons and the picture they inserted.

name: Batuque
tagline: Watch and hear the rhythms of Pernambuco, one drum at a time, then all together.
description: An animated show of one to two minutes for each rhythm of Pernambuco: maracatu de baque virado, coco, frevo, forró pé-de-serra, manguebeat, brega and bregafunk. A wheel shows the beats of each instrument with the score underneath, every sound is a public-domain recording of a real instrument, and a show can be exported as a vertical video made in the browser.

name: Leve
tagline: Today's time and events in the macOS menu bar, so deep focus never costs a meeting.
description: The menu bar says "Free until 2:00 PM", "in 12 min" or "20 min left", never the event's name, so it is safe on a shared screen. A notification arrives a few minutes before each event, a calm full-screen alert with a Join button covers every display just before it starts, and Leve says the time on the half hour. It reads today's events only and never changes a calendar.

name: Trickle Tabs
tagline: Keeps Brave fast when you open many tabs: background tabs load only when you open them.
description: Each new background tab waits in a queue, loads only until its title and icon appear, and loads for real when you open it. A tab nobody looked at for ten minutes goes to sleep, sooner when memory is low, while the tab in view, tabs playing sound, pinned tabs and chat and mail sites stay awake. It runs in Brave on macOS.
note: Not published yet. This page says what it does.

name: DELE Diario
tagline: Daily iPhone practice with the real task types of DELE C1, DELE C2 and CCSE.
description: Each exercise is a real exam task in its official format, corrected at the end, and every mistake comes back in a spaced review until it is learned. A notebook keeps saved phrases, and statistics follow each task type. Everything stays on the iPhone, with no account and no server; an optional AI estimate sends a text to Anthropic only with your own key and only when you ask.
note: A personal study app, not published. This page says what it does.

name: Panoram
tagline: Messaging, email, tasks and AI in one native macOS window, through Matrix.
description: One place for every conversation and every task: WhatsApp, Telegram, Instagram, Messenger, LinkedIn, Microsoft Teams, Gmail threads, TikTok messages and Todoist lists in one macOS app, connected through Matrix. The direction is provider-neutral and local-first, and most of it is not built yet.
note: A personal app, not published. This page says what it does.

name: Workbench
tagline: Safety-bounded engineering workflows for coding agents, as skills for Claude Code.
description: Recurring project work turned into named workflows a coding agent can run: setting up a repository, turning an idea into issues, planning and implementing them, reviewing, auditing and releasing. Each workflow has one owner, a narrow trigger and a hard limit on what it may change, and merging stays the developer's decision. Many skills began in other open-source projects, and every source is credited.
note: Private. This page is its only public description.
